# Games

*Page PDF 24*

## **Games**
Many taverns keep the equipment needed to run a certain game on the premises. The GM should decide if any of the customers in the taproom are looking for a game or would be willing to play if asked. An unwilling customer might be willing to play a game if a Character asks them and passes a Charm Test (use the difficulty modifier to Gossip Tests for the purposes of Charm Tests). 

Most games are played for stakes determined by the status of the venue. A typical stake will be three pennies in a Brass Tier Venue, two shillings in a Silver Tier venue, and a Gold Crown in a Gold Tier venue. A Character who wants to play for fun, or for extra money, may make appropriate Charm or Haggle Tests, but if such tests are failed, they may be viewed as either a hustler or a time waster by other customers. 

Full rules and descriptions for these games can be found in **Rough Nights & Hard Days** . The rules given here are quick abstract versions. 

## **Discouraged**
Not only does this tavern not provide any equipment for games, but the landlord actively discourages competition. They may regard games as too déclassé for their establishment, too likely to result in brawls, or a form of immoral behaviour in and of themselves. If customers insist on playing a game, members of staff in the same room may take a Perception Test every 10 Rounds to spot them and will ask gamers to either desist or leave once they are spotted. 

## **None**
There are no special facilities at the tavern for games, but if customers bring their own, the bar staff probably won’t object. 

## **Al-Zahr**
A simple dice game. 2 dice are rolled, with participants trying to achieve a target number. To play, decide on players, add stakes to the pot for each player, first player chooses a number between 7 and 15, the players take turns to roll, and the first player to roll the target or 20 wins the pot. 

## **Alvatafl**
A chess-like game in which a besieging army of 48 Dwarf pieces take on a centrally placed army of 12 Elves. Players should make **Challenging (+0) Intelligence** or **Lore (Warfare)** Tests each turn, and total their SL. The first player to reach 10 SL or roll a Critical success wins. If both players achieve the victory condition in the same turn, the game is a draw. 

## **Arm Wrestling**
No equipment is needed to arm wrestle, though it may be discouraged as coarse behaviour in Gold Tier venues. Players make **Extended Opposed Challenging (+0) Strength** Tests. The first Character to 10 SL wins. In case of a draw, the game goes to the Character with the highest Strength. 

## **Beast Among the Tailors**
16 skittles are set up, and a participant may take up to three attempts to knock them down with a metal ball swinging on the end of a chain. Participants may make up to three **Average (+20) Ballistic Skill** Tests. The total SL indicates the number of skittles knocked down. 

## **Bowls**
Usually played in the tavern yard or beer garden. Players take three **Challenging (+0) Ballistic Skill** or **Ranged (Throwing)** Tests, recording their total SL. The highest SL wins the game. 

## **Cerevis**
A drinking game played with cards. An alternative vocabulary must be adopted, and players who lose a round earn a mark called an ‘owl’. Each turn an **Average (+20) Combined Gamble and Initiative** Test is required from all players. The lowest score on the Gamble Test earns an owl. The lowest score on the Initiative Test forgets the alternative vocabulary and must forfeit. For every forfeit, a player must drink a pint of beer. They may also drink a pint to erase an owl. By the time everyone is bored of the game the player with the fewest owls wins. 

## **Darts**
Each Round, each player makes three **Challenging (+0) Ballistic Skill** or **Ranged (Throwing)** Tests. If the test is successful, record the number thrown on the dice. Total these numbers up. The first player to reach 501 wins the game. 

## **Dominos**
Each player makes an **Opposed Average (+20) Gambling** Test. In case of a draw, the lowest number wins the game. 

## **Mühlen**
A 2-player game in which nine pieces are moved about on a grid. Players should make **Extended Opposed Easy (+40) Intelligence** Tests. The first player to reach 9 or more SL wins. If both players reach 9 or more SL on the same Turn, the game is a draw. 

## **Scarlet Empress**
The most popular card game in the Empire. To play, everyone adds a stake to the pot and makes an **Average (+20) Gambling** Test. A clear winner wins the pot. On a draw, players either add another stake or retire from the game. 

## **Stones**
A popular game for two to four players where stones of different sizes are moved about on an octagonal board. Players should make **Extended Opposed Average (+20) Intelligence** Tests. The first player to reach 10 or more SL wins. If both players reach 10 or more SL on the same Turn, the game is a draw.
